references.name: Edward Thorp
references.desc: Beat the Dealer, Beat the Market; co-invented first wearable computer with Claude Shannon; pioneer of quantitative trading and convertible arbitrage

references.name: Claude Shannon
references.desc: Father of information theory; co-built roulette-beating computer with Thorp at MIT

references.name: George Soros
references.desc: Reflexivity theory — markets shape fundamentals, not just reflect them; legendary macro trader

references.name: Gustave Le Bon
references.desc: The Crowd — psychology of herd behavior; kept alongside Schwager's books by Ed Seykota

references.name: Charles Mackay
references.desc: Extraordinary Popular Delusions and the Madness of Crowds — classic on speculative manias

references.name: Marty Schwartz
references.desc: Pit trader who taught: "Don't average losing trades. Be smaller than you need to be. Take profits."

references.name: John Kelly
references.desc: Kelly Criterion for optimal position sizing; "Half Kelly" gives 75% of the return with half the volatility

references.name: Leda Braga
references.desc: Built BlueCrest's systematic research team; demonstrated that static trading systems eventually degrade

references.name: Bernie Madoff
references.desc: History's largest Ponzi scheme; Thorp was likely first to uncover the fraud years before Markopolos

references.name: Michael Milken
references.desc: Junk bond king; prosecution of Thorp's partner was widely assumed to be leverage against Milken

references.name: Joel Greenblatt
references.desc: Value investor profiled in the book; The Little Book That Beats the Market

references.name: Ray Dalio
references.desc: Bridgewater Associates founder; systematic macro approach and "radical transparency" culture

connections.author: Edward O. Thorp & Sheen T. Kassouf
